requirements: Run the named suites and verify all six new CloudSolrClientCacheTest methods execute and pass: test503DoesNotReplayCompletedRoutedUpdates, test503RetryRespectsV2SkipRetry, test503RetriesEligibleRead, test503RouteExceptionRetainsExistingRetry, test503DoesNotReplayUnspecifiedRequest, and test503MarkedQueryDoesNotRetry. Record individual test counts, skips, failures, fresh XML and logs. The replay test mocks the LB client and counts routed submissions; it is not proof of persisted index state or real HTTP behavior.

In a separate disposable checkout at the exact reviewed PR head dfde089fd9dd0e5e79774593e66dd030e1b7dd22, bring over only the unchanged CloudSolrClientCacheTest.java from a020611b228b02af90b2a80ef92fe95f463b4e81. Run test503DoesNotReplayCompletedRoutedUpdates and test503RetryRespectsV2SkipRetry with the same seed and record actual assertion failures on the original PR production code, then run the same methods at the fix head and require passes. Compilation, harness setup, timeouts or skipped tests do not count as fail-before behavior. Preserve logs and fresh XML for both legs.

The new generic-write regression test503DoesNotReplayUnspecifiedRequest must fail by assertion with the unchanged tests on the earlier 9add678bd94b8c6f1b119535583e8ac8b0deea90 production code and pass at this head. Check that the new 503 path only retries QUERY-typed requests, that a marked query does not retry, and that the earlier RouteException and communication-error paths are not presented as fixed. The generic-request test stubs sendRequest and does not prove actual LB or HTTP behavior.

Run tidy and require no tracked file changes. If formatting changes files, stop and hand back: commit and a superseding exact-head gate are required. Run root check -x test without silent exclusions. Diagnose executed failures before any retry and distinguish environment failures from code or test failures.

Review and report the material design limitation: newly broadened 503 retry is limited to QUERY-typed requests because a 503 alone does not prove that no update was applied. Therefore this follow-up does not fix the original graceful-shutdown indexing case; it preserves the pre-existing RouteException and communication-error retry policies, whose partial-update safety is not established by this gate. A green gate proves only the stated changes, not general exactly-once behavior or end-to-end graceful-shutdown recovery.

Publish a receipt with exact head, all commands, exit codes, test counts, skips, fresh XML and log locations, baseline results, formatting status, and limitations. Mark incomplete or failed for any missing proof leg or unresolved failure. Release the claim only with executor-stop evidence.
